Definition: from G4073 and G1491; rock-like, i.e. rocky:--stony.
BiblicalUsage: Petrodes means rocky, stony, and it describes the ground in the parable of the sower. Some seed fell upon stony places, where it had not much earth, and it sprang up quickly, but because it had no depth of earth it withered when the sun rose.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that stony ground is the hearer who receives the word with joy but has no root in himself: quick to spring up, and quick to wither when trouble comes.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
